rows.text: The draw engine and the threats are the same cards. Every enchantment you cast draws you one card off Sythis, another off each enchantress effect on the battlefield, and gains life on the way. With three of them out a two-mana Aura is four cards, and the deck simply never runs out. Note the land count is deliberately low — the mana comes from Auras on lands and from Sanctum Weaver, not from drawing more Forests.

guide.title: The commander and the enchantress stack

rows.name: Sythis, Harvest's Hand
rows.text: two mana, and every enchantment spell is a card and a life. She is cheap enough to recast through removal all game.

rows.name: Argothian Enchantress
rows.text: the best of the redundant copies, because SHROUD means she cannot be answered by targeted removal at all.

rows.name: Mesa Enchantress
rows.text: another card per enchantment.

rows.name: Satyr Enchanter
rows.text: and another.

rows.name: Enchantress's Presence
rows.text: the same effect on an enchantment, so it triggers everything else when you cast it.

rows.name: Eidolon of Blossoms
rows.text: constellation, so it draws off enchantments that ENTER rather than are cast — which catches Replenish and every token-generated Aura.

rows.name: Setessan Champion
rows.text: draws and grows on every enchantment that enters.

rows.name: Kor Spiritdancer
rows.text: draws on Aura spells specifically, and gets +2/+2 per Aura attached to her.

rows.name: Femeref Enchantress
rows.text: a card whenever an enchantment hits a graveyard, which turns their removal into your card advantage.

rows.name: Sanctum Weaver
rows.text: taps for one mana per enchantment you control. On a developed board that is six or eight mana from a two-drop.

rows.name: Fertile Ground
rows.text: an extra mana of any colour off a land, and it is an enchantment so it draws.

rows.name: Overgrowth
rows.text: two extra green off one land.

rows.name: Abundant Growth
rows.text: fixes and replaces itself immediately.

rows.name: Nylea's Presence
rows.text: makes a land every basic type, and draws.

rows.name: Herald of the Pantheon
rows.text: enchantments cost one less and gain you a life each.

rows.name: Danitha Capashen, Paragon
rows.text: Auras cost one less, on a lifelinking first striker.

rows.name: Land Tax
rows.text: this deck is deliberately land-light, so an opponent almost always has more. Three basics a turn is free fuel.

rows.name: Mirri's Guile
rows.text: sets the top three every upkeep, which with this much draw means you never miss.

rows.name: Greater Auramancy
rows.text: your other enchantments have SHROUD, and enchanted creatures have shroud too. It is the single most important protection card in the deck.

rows.name: Privileged Position
rows.text: hexproof for every other permanent you control.

rows.name: Karmic Justice
rows.text: if they destroy a noncreature permanent of yours, you destroy any permanent of theirs. It stops targeted enchantment removal before it starts.

rows.name: Destiny Spinner
rows.text: your creature and enchantment spells cannot be countered, and it animates a land as an X/X where X is your enchantment count.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: shroud and haste for whichever creature is carrying the Auras.

rows.name: Replenish
rows.text: returns EVERY enchantment from your graveyard to the battlefield. It is the answer to a wrath, and in this deck it usually returns six or more cards at once.

rows.name: Ancestral Mask
rows.text: +2/+2 for each other enchantment ON THE BATTLEFIELD — including your opponents'. It routinely reads +20/+20.

rows.name: Ethereal Armor
rows.text: +1/+1 per enchantment you control, plus first strike.

rows.name: All That Glitters
rows.text: the same count including artifacts.

rows.name: Daybreak Coronet
rows.text: +3/+3, first strike, vigilance and lifelink for two mana, as long as another Aura is already there.

rows.name: Kor Spiritdancer
rows.text: the natural carrier — she grows on her own and draws every time you suit her up.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with your commander out, take both halves. Double strike on an Ancestral Mask creature ends the game; protection from every colour makes it unblockable and unkillable at the same time.

rows.name: Archon of Sun's Grace
rows.text: a 2/2 flying lifelinking Pegasus for every enchantment that enters. This deck plays thirty of them.

rows.name: Hallowed Haunting
rows.text: a Spirit for every enchantment you CAST, each one as big as your Spirit count, and at seven enchantments they all fly and have vigilance.

rows.name: Luminarch Ascension
rows.text: with Ghostly Prison out you rarely lose life, so the counters accumulate for free and then it makes a 4/4 flier every turn.

rows.name: Destiny Spinner
rows.text: turns a land into a surprise attacker sized by your enchantment count.

rows.name: Ghostly Prison
rows.text: they pay {2} per attacker or go hit somebody else. In a deck with no early blockers this buys the turns you need.

rows.name: Grasp of Fate
rows.text: exiles a nonland permanent from EACH opponent, on one enchantment that also draws you cards.

rows.name: Aura of Silence
rows.text: taxes their artifacts and enchantments two, then eats one.

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: every creature you play destroys an artifact or enchantment. Alongside Archon of Sun's Grace making a Pegasus per enchantment, this is a removal engine.

rows.name: Kenrith's Transformation
rows.text: turns their commander into a vanilla 3/3 Elk and draws you a card.

rows.name: Path to Exile
rows.text: one mana, exile.

rows.name: Beast Within
rows.text: any permanent, at instant speed.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: the white copy.

rows.name: Idyllic Tutor
rows.text: any enchantment in the deck — usually Greater Auramancy, Grasp of Fate or Hallowed Haunting.

rows.name: Open the Armory
rows.text: any Aura, which usually means Ancestral Mask.

rows.name: Heliod's Pilgrim
rows.text: the same on a body, and it triggers constellation effects when Auras come down later.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep an enchantress and a cheap enchantment. Sythis on turn two into a one- or two-mana Aura on turn three is how the engine starts; a hand of expensive payoffs with no draw engine stalls out.
Deploy the draw engines before the payoffs. An extra enchantress on the battlefield multiplies every card you cast for the rest of the game; an extra Aura does not.

rows.name: Greater Auramancy
rows.text: get it down before you commit an Ancestral Mask to a creature. Without it, one removal spell in response to the Aura two-for-ones you.

rows.name: Argothian Enchantress
rows.text: she has shroud, so she survives everything except a wrath. If you have a choice of which enchantress to play into open mana, play her.
